Beautiful descriptions of marriage in the Quran appears in Surah Arghum, verse 21.
Allah tells us that amongst his signs is that he created spouses
so that we may find tranquility in them and that he places affection and mercy between them.
This verse introduces three essential pillars of marriage.
The first is sakina, which means tranquility.
Think about what tranquility means in a relationship.
It means feeling emotionally secure, knowing that you can express your thoughts
without fear or humiliation and trusting that your spouse will treat you with dignity and respect.
A peaceful marriage does not mean that disagreements never happen.
It means that even when difficulties arise,
both individuals are committed to resolving them without causing unnecessary harm.
The second pillar is mawuddha or affection.
Affection is more than simply telling someone that you love them.
It is demonstrated through everyday actions.
A kind word, a thoughtful gesture, showing appreciation, spending meaningful time together
or offering support after a difficult day.
These small acts strengthen emotional connection.
The third pillar is rahmah, meaning mercy.
Mercy becomes particularly important when life is challenging.
There will be times when one spouse is tired, unwell, worried or struggling.
During these moments compassion and understanding can make an enormous difference.
Marriage requires us to recognise that our spouse is human with strengths, weaknesses,
